question: What is the primary goal of patient safety in healthcare?

options.B: Reducing the number of hired staff

explanation: Patient safety focuses directly on avoiding and preventing any accidental injury or harm to individuals while they are receiving medical treatment. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h1)

question: Why are nurses often referred to as the final safety net in clinical care?

options.A: They write all the hospital safety policies and clinical guidelines
options.B: They pay for any financial penalties resulting from medical mistakes
options.C: They have the legal authority to fire negligent doctors
options.D: They are the last healthcare workers to catch errors before harm occurs

explanation: Because nurses spend the most continuous time at the bedside, they are uniquely positioned to double-check orders and catch mistakes right before they affect the patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h1)

question: What does the Swiss Cheese Model of safety explain?

options.A: How hospital kitchens prevent foodborne bacterial illnesses
options.B: The best dietary guidelines for recovering hospital patients
options.C: The step-by-step process of cleaning surgical instruments
options.D: How multiple system failures align to cause an accident

explanation: Think of safety layers like slices of Swiss cheese. Accidents only happen when the holes in every single slice line up at the same time! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h2)

question: Why do safety frameworks focus on system design instead of just blaming the nurse?

options.A: Human error is often triggered by poor processes and workplace design
options.B: Blaming workers is illegal under international labor laws
options.C: Workers never make mistakes if they receive basic orientation
options.D: Systems are easier to replace than trained clinical personnel

explanation: Even great nurses make mistakes when processes are confusing or the ward is chaotic. Fixing the system stops errors before they start! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h2)

question: Which of the following is a common category of clinical safety risk?
explanation: Giving the wrong drug, dose, or time is one of the most frequent and dangerous safety risks encountered in everyday clinical practice. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h3)

question: A patient with unsteady balance and dizziness is admitted to the medical ward. What is the most immediate safety risk to prevent?

options.C: A physical fall leading to injury

explanation: Unsteadiness and dizziness directly increase the likelihood of slips and falls, making fall precautions the priority intervention for this patient. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h3)

question: Which condition is a major safety risk specifically related to maternity care?
explanation: Excessive bleeding after childbirth is one of the leading preventable causes of maternal mortality worldwide, requiring strict monitoring and rapid response. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why is patient safety in maternity care uniquely complex?

options.A: Pregnancy completely prevents any physical or medical complications
options.B: The nurse must monitor and protect two distinct lives at the same time
options.C: Labor and delivery wards never experience staffing shortages
options.D: Maternity patients never follow clinical instructions or take medications

explanation: In maternity care, you are caring for both the mother and the baby. That doubles your watch duty and your clinical responsibility! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h4)

question: What is the main purpose of an incident report in a healthcare facility?

options.A: To provide permanent legal evidence for the patient's court case
options.B: To document safety events and improve institutional systems
options.C: To formally punish the specific nurse who made the mistake
options.D: To calculate the daily patient feeding and laundry costs

explanation: Incident reports aren't for witch hunts! They are learning tools to help the hospital spot recurring issues and make the ward safer for everyone. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h5)

question: How does a Root Cause Analysis differ from simply blaming an individual worker?

options.A: It focuses exclusively on financial losses rather than clinical outcomes
options.B: It investigates underlying systemic flaws rather than stopping at personal fault
options.C: It ensures that the guilty employee is fired immediately without appeal
options.D: It hides safety mistakes from hospital management and regulatory bodies

explanation: Root Cause Analysis asks 'Why did this happen?' instead of 'Who did this?'. It digs deep into workflow, equipment, and communication to fix the real problem. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h5)

question: What does the acronym SBAR stand for in clinical communication?
explanation: SBAR is a standardized communication tool that helps healthcare workers share critical patient information clearly and concisely during handovers. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h6)

question: A nurse is about to administer a high-alert medication like IV heparin. What should be done first?

options.A: Waiting until the end of the shift to document the administration
options.B: An independent double-check of the dose with another qualified nurse
options.C: Asking the patient to guess what the medication is used for
options.D: Hiding the medication package so other staff members cannot see it

explanation: High-alert drugs can easily cause severe harm if miscalculated. Always get a second nurse to independently verify the dose before giving it! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h6)

question: What is the main characteristic of a 'just culture' in healthcare?

options.A: Allowing patients to manage their own hospital medication schedules
options.B: Punishing every single mistake severely regardless of the cause
options.C: Balancing individual accountability with systemic error analysis
options.D: Ignoring minor errors to keep staff morale high and positive

explanation: A just culture means you can speak up and report mistakes honestly without fear of unfair punishment, while still holding everyone reasonably accountable. [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h7)

question: Why is psychological safety so important for nurses on the ward?

options.A: It allows nurses to skip mandatory documentation and charting duties
options.B: It gives them the confidence to speak up about safety hazards without fear
options.C: It completely eliminates all physical stress and burnout on the ward
options.D: It prevents patients from asking difficult questions about their care

explanation: When nurses feel psychologically safe, they won't hesitate to question a dodgy doctor's order or report a near-miss, and that saves lives! [learn more](GNS312_U5_T5#GNS312_U5_T5_h7)
